title: Bhooth Bangla Just Crossed ₹266 Crore. Akshay Kumar Is Officially Back.
excerpt: A horror-comedy directed by Priyadarshan has become Akshay's second-highest domestic earner post-COVID — and it's still selling tickets in its seventh week.
body:
Here is a sentence nobody would have written eighteen months ago: Akshay Kumar is having the best theatrical run of his post-COVID career, and he did it by going back to ghosts.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=XW1RkKiRnsg

Bhooth Bangla has crossed ₹266 crore worldwide. Let that number sit for a moment. This is a horror-comedy — not a franchise sequel, not an IP extension, not a "universe" film — just a straightforward ghost-in-a-mansion movie directed by Priyadarshan, starring Akshay Kumar, and relying on the radical proposition that audiences still want to laugh in a theatre.

They do. They desperately do.

"The horror-comedy genre still has massive pull if the content connects with the ground audience." — Sacnilk trade analysis, June 10, 2026

The domestic net stands at ₹179.85 crore, just a whisper away from the ₹180 crore mark. When it crosses — and it will, probably by tomorrow — Bhooth Bangla becomes Akshay Kumar's second-highest domestic earner in the post-pandemic era, behind only Sooryavanshi (₹195.55 crore). To put that in context, it has already surpassed Housefull 5 domestically (₹183.38 crore at gross level), and left OMG 2 (₹151 crore) and Jolly LLB 3 (₹117 crore) well behind.

The overseas tally sits at a respectable ₹53.75 crore — not blockbuster territory for the diaspora market, but solid for a film that doesn't have "Khan" in the title or a Marvel-sized marketing budget. The combined worldwide gross of ₹266.81 crore makes Bhooth Bangla one of the most profitable Bollywood films of 2026, given its moderate production budget.

The Priyadarshan Effect

Here's what everyone already knows but keeps forgetting: Akshay Kumar is at his best when Priyadarshan is behind the camera. The duo gave Indian cinema Hera Pheri, Bhool Bhulaiyaa, Garam Masala, and Bhagam Bhag — films that didn't just work at the box office but became permanent fixtures in the cultural vocabulary of every Indian household. "Ae Baburao" isn't a line. It's a lifestyle.

Bhooth Bangla isn't trying to reinvent anything. It's a haunted-house comedy built on timing, physical gags, and the chemistry between Akshay and a well-calibrated ensemble. Priyadarshan understands something that several of Akshay's recent directors have not: the man is a comedian first, an action star second, and a message-movie vehicle never.

The films that nearly sank Akshay's career — Selfiee, Bade Miyan Chote Miyan, Khel Khel Mein — all had one thing in common. They tried to make him something he isn't. Bhooth Bangla made him exactly what he is.

https://www.instagram.com/p/DXJAF75jW-F/

Seven Weeks and Still Going

The most remarkable thing about Bhooth Bangla's run isn't the opening weekend (which was strong but not earth-shattering). It's the legs. The film sold 8,280 tickets on BookMyShow on its seventh Monday alone. Total platform bookings have crossed 33.60 lakh tickets. That kind of sustained footfall suggests the film has crossed over from "opening weekend crowd" to "family outing" territory — the holy grail of Hindi commercial cinema.

This is the audience that doesn't care about Twitter discourse or teaser view counts. They show up on Saturday evening with their kids, buy samosas in the interval, and tell their friends at work on Monday. Bhooth Bangla found them, and they found it right back.

What This Means for the Diaspora

For NRIs who've watched Akshay Kumar cycle through increasingly forgettable theatrical releases over the last three years, Bhooth Bangla is a reminder of why he was a superstar in the first place. And if you missed it in theatres — which, let's be honest, most of the diaspora did because the initial overseas prints were limited — it hits Netflix on June 12.

Mark it. This is the easiest recommendation of the month. Two hours of Akshay doing what he does best, in a genre that Priyadarshan owns, with the kind of comic timing that no amount of CGI or "Spy Universe" branding can manufacture.

The Comeback Nobody Planned

Akshay Kumar didn't hold a press conference announcing a career pivot. He didn't rebrand. He didn't sign with a new agency or start a podcast about mental health. He just made a horror-comedy with his favourite director and let the audience decide.

They decided ₹266 crore worth of yes.

With the Netflix premiere imminent and the theatrical run still holding, Bhooth Bangla's final worldwide number could creep towards ₹280-290 crore. Whether it gets there or not, the film has already done something more valuable: it has reminded the industry that Akshay Kumar works when you let Akshay Kumar be Akshay Kumar. Someone write that on a whiteboard in every producer's office.
